motivation: Strategic disruption and destructive operations against government and critical infrastructure targets aligned with Russian state objectives.
sector_targeting: Electric power, government, and other critical infrastructure, including repeated operations against Ukraine's electricity sector.

signature_ttp.stat_line: Used the MicroSCADA SCIL-API during the 2022 Ukraine electric-power attack to issue unauthorized commands to substation devices.

rms_relevance: An RMS that accepts network commands could face manipulated device behavior or configuration, but no cited source establishes Sandworm targeting an RMS; this connection is theoretical.
provenance: MITRE ATT&CK, Sandworm Team (G0034), group description and ICS technique T1692.001 procedure for the 2022 Ukraine Electric Power Attack.
what_this_card_cannot_tell_you: The card does not establish that every alias represents exactly the same operators, that Sandworm has targeted an RMS, or that its electric-grid techniques would work unchanged against nuclear radiation-monitoring equipment.
visual_concept: A black sandstorm spiraling around an abstract electrical substation sigil; no person, face, portrait, or likeness.

assessed_affiliation: Russian government cyber activity according to CISA and FBI reporting; vendor naming and group boundaries overlap and are not exact.
motivation: Cyberespionage, credential collection, and preparation of access to energy-sector networks and industrial environments.
sector_targeting: Energy-sector organizations, ICS equipment providers, and industrial software users.

signature_ttp.stat_line: Trojanized legitimate software packages hosted on compromised ICS equipment-provider websites.

rms_relevance: Compromised software from an RMS or industrial-monitoring supplier could introduce malicious code into a plant environment, but no cited source establishes Dragonfly targeting RMS products; this connection is theoretical.
provenance: MITRE ATT&CK, Dragonfly (G0035), group description; MITRE ATT&CK for ICS, T0862 Supply Chain Compromise, Dragonfly procedure example; Symantec, Dragonfly: Cyberespionage Attacks Against Energy Suppliers, July 7, 2014.
what_this_card_cannot_tell_you: The card cannot reconcile every vendor alias or prove that all activity labeled Dragonfly came from one team. It also does not establish compromise of an RMS product or a nuclear facility.
visual_concept: A mechanical dragonfly perched on a sealed software crate with a broken integrity stamp; no person, face, portrait, or likeness.

assessed_affiliation: CISA, FBI, NSA, EPA, and partner agencies describe CyberAv3ngers as an Iranian Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps-affiliated cyber persona. The hacktivist actor_type records the persona's public presentation; the assessed state affiliation is recorded separately.
motivation: Publicly presented ideological retaliation against Israeli-made technology and symbolic defacement; government reporting assesses an IRGC affiliation.
sector_targeting: Internet-exposed Unitronics PLCs and HMIs in water, energy, food and beverage, transportation, healthcare, and other sectors.

signature_ttp.stat_line: Authenticated to internet-connected Unitronics devices that used default or no passwords, then altered device operation and displayed defacement messages.

rms_relevance: An internet-accessible RMS component retaining default credentials would present a comparable access condition, but no cited source establishes CyberAv3ngers targeting an RMS; this connection is theoretical.
provenance: CISA et al., AA23-335A, IRGC-Affiliated Cyber Actors Exploit PLCs in Multiple Sectors, Overview, Background Information, and Threat Actor Activity Against U.S.-Based Unitronics Devices.
what_this_card_cannot_tell_you: The card cannot independently verify the IRGC affiliation, determine which public attack claims were genuine, or show that CyberAv3ngers targeted an RMS or nuclear organization.
visual_concept: A cracked PLC screen bearing an abstract lightning emblem and an exposed default-password key; no person, face, portrait, or likeness.

assessed_affiliation: The FBI described DarkSide as a Russia-based cybercrime group operating a ransomware-as-a-service model; this is a criminal classification, not an attribution to the Russian state.
motivation: Financial extortion through ransomware and ransom collection.
sector_targeting: Organizations across critical-infrastructure sectors, including the energy sector and Colonial Pipeline.

signature_ttp.stat_line: DarkSide ransomware affected Colonial Pipeline's IT network and led to a precautionary operational shutdown; CISA reported no indication that OT was directly affected.

rms_relevance: Ransomware affecting supporting IT or monitoring services could indirectly interrupt RMS data availability or reporting, but the Colonial incident does not demonstrate DarkSide access to OT or RMS equipment; this connection is theoretical.
provenance: CISA and FBI, AA21-131A, Darkside Ransomware: Best Practices for Preventing Business Disruption from Ransomware Attacks, Summary; FBI, Statement on Compromise of Colonial Pipeline Networks, May 10, 2021; CISA, FBI, and NSA, AA21-291A, Overview; MITRE ATT&CK for ICS, T0828 Loss of Productivity and Revenue, Colonial Pipeline example.
what_this_card_cannot_tell_you: The card does not identify every DarkSide affiliate or prove that DarkSide reached Colonial Pipeline's OT network. CISA and FBI reported no indication that OT was directly affected.
visual_concept: A dark pipeline valve wrapped in a padlock chain and interrupted currency waveform; no person, face, portrait, or likeness.

assessed_affiliation: Former contractor employee with knowledge of the Maroochy wastewater control system; no state or organized-crime affiliation is established in the cited case study.
motivation: Personal grievance and retaliation after employment and contracting disputes, as described in the public case study.
sector_targeting: Maroochy Shire wastewater pumping stations and their radio-controlled management system.

signature_ttp.stat_line: Used a two-way radio system and engineering knowledge to send false data and instructions to pumping stations and the central computer.

rms_relevance: A knowledgeable insider with authorized knowledge or portable engineering equipment could misuse an RMS maintenance interface, but no cited source connects this actor to an RMS or nuclear facility; this connection is theoretical.
provenance: MITRE ATT&CK, Maroochy Water Breach (C0020), campaign dates and ICS technique T1692.001; Marshall Abrams, Malicious Control System Cyber Security Attack Case Study: Maroochy Water Services, Australia, July 23, 2008.
what_this_card_cannot_tell_you: The card describes one documented insider incident and cannot establish that the same radio path, engineering access, motive, or control architecture exists in an RMS or nuclear facility.
visual_concept: An unmanned radio transmitter sending false waveforms toward abstract pump and sensor symbols; do not depict the named individual or any human figure.
